issues.legal_issue: A trial decree merges into the appellate decree when the entire decree is appealed and the appellate court decides the appeal on its merits, even if it affirms the lower court’s decision.
material_facts: A decree for possession was passed in a suit based solely on rent default.
The entire decree was appealed through the lower appellate court to the High Court.
The High Court heard the appeal on its merits and affirmed the decree, while allowing additional time to vacate.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s decree merged into the High Court’s decree, which became the operative decree capable of execution.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of merger rests on the principle that there cannot be more than one operative order governing the same subject matter. When an appeal is decided on its merits, the appellate decree is operative even if it merely affirms the trial decree. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Amritlal Bhogilal & Co., Collector of Customs v. East India Commercial Co. Ltd., Jowad Hussain v. Gendan Singh, Bhup Inder v. Bijai, and Brij Narain v. Tejpal. It distinguished State of U.P. v. Mohammad Nooh and State of Madras v. Madurai Mills Co. Ltd. on their facts and the scope of the proceedings involved.

rule.if: civil_decree_appeal and entire_decree_appealed and same_subject_matter and appellate_court_heard_appeal_on_merits

predicates.civil_decree_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a civil case involving a decree.
predicates.entire_decree_appealed: The appellant challenged the entire decree rather than only a distinct part of it.
predicates.same_subject_matter: The appeal and the original case concern the same subject matter.
predicates.appellate_court_heard_appeal_on_merits: The appellate court considered and decided the appeal on its merits.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges the entire decree concerning the same subject matter and is decided on its merits, the trial decree merges into the appellate decree.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory tenant-relief remedy limited to decrees passed before a specified commencement date cannot set aside a later appellate decree that is the operative decree for execution.
material_facts: The decree for possession was based solely on the tenant’s default in paying rent, and possession had not been recovered.
The entire decree was appealed, and the High Court decided the appeal on its merits after the statutory eligibility cutoff, affirming the decree with additional time to vacate.
The tenant applied under the statutory relief provision to set aside the decree.
The Supreme Court held that the High Court decree was the only decree capable of execution.
issues.conclusion: The statutory relief provision did not apply because the operative appellate decree was passed after the relevant commencement date and could not be set aside under that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17D of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, as introduced by the 1969 amendment, allowed relief for qualifying possession decrees passed before the commencement of the 1968 amendment, where possession had not been recovered. The decree the provision can set aside is the operative decree capable of execution. Where the entire decree is appealed and the appeal is decided on its merits, that is the appellate decree. The Court relied on Jowad Hussain v. Gendan Singh, Bhup Inder v. Bijai, Brij Narain v. Tejpal, and the merger principles discussed in Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay v. Amritlal Bhogilal & Co. and Collector of Customs v. East India Commercial Co. Ltd.

rule.if: tenant_relief_application and eviction_for_rent_default_only and possession_not_recovered and full_decree_appealed and appellate_court_heard_appeal_on_merits and appellate_decree_is_operative and operative_decree_outside_eligible_period

predicates.tenant_relief_application: A tenant applies for statutory relief to set aside a decree for recovery of possession.
predicates.eviction_for_rent_default_only: The possession decree was based only on the tenant’s default in paying rent.
predicates.possession_not_recovered: The landlord had not recovered possession by executing the decree.
predicates.full_decree_appealed: The entire possession decree was appealed.
predicates.appellate_court_heard_appeal_on_merits: The appellate court heard and decided the appeal on its merits.
predicates.appellate_decree_is_operative: The appellate decree is the decree capable of execution in the case.
predicates.operative_decree_outside_eligible_period: The operative decree was made outside the period for which the statutory relief is available.

issues.definition: If a tenant seeks statutory relief from a rent-default possession decree, possession remains unrecovered, the full decree was decided on appeal, and the operative appellate decree falls outside the eligible period, the relief cannot set aside that decree.
